utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Please be seated. Good morning to the technical booth, the interpreters, the Registry staff, counsel for the Prosecution, counsel for the Defence. We will resume our hearing, and it is up to Mr. Stojanovic to tell us what we are going to do today.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, good morning. With your permission, we will continue with the testimony of witnesses. However, I would like to ask for a clarification of a decision of yours. We have received your ruling about the videolink for our witnesses scheduled for the 18th and 19th of April. Five witnesses have been planned for the videolink. At the same time, we have envisaged four witnesses in the courtroom here. So could you assist us? Will that be feasible, and how?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will look into that after the break, because I do not have the information at hand, and I will let you know after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The Defence calls its next witness. It is a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Pardon me for interrupting, Your Honour. I just wanted, in order so there is no interruption in the flow of witnesses, I just wanted to remind my learned friend that we do not have identities on certain pseudonym witnesses, so it could affect cross-examination if things move slowly - I'm sorry - quickly: DD/5, 7, 4, 8, and 3. If that could be remedied before the end of the day, we can make sure there will no problem. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I respond? Your Honour, by the end of the day we will be in the courtroom, so I doubt that we will have time. This obviously applies to our obligation which begins to run from the 9th of April, and I think that we will certainly observe the minimum term of eight days -- seven days regarding the disclosure of the identity of those witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, DD/5 is number seventh witness, so if we move, we simply have no information on this individual. I think that will be a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is a witness who has been scheduled for the 9th of April, so during this week certainly, maybe even tomorrow, we will be able to disclose his identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, then. Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If this is counsel's representation, then I will have to accept it and just see how it goes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stojanovic, I think we discussed this request for protective measures. The question was raised and you took upon yourself the obligation to communicate the identity of the witnesses. So it's up to you. If the witnesses arrive and the conditions have not been met, you will be creating a problem, so you will have to disclose the identity within the time limit envisaged. So let us begin. Which witness are you calling, Mr. Stojanovic? Who is your next witness?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Our next witness is a protected witness with a pseudonym DD/1, and my co-counsel, Mr. Deretic, will be conducting the examination-in-chief. Could the witness be brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness DD/1. Can you hear me? Can you hear me? Are you hearing me? Are you listening to me? Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's fine. Please read the solemn declaration given to you by the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for coming. You will now be answering questions put to you by Mr. Deretic first, and after that, there will come questions by the Prosecutor and the Judges as well. Mr. Deretic, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me for a moment. Before we begin, I think we need to show the witness a piece of paper with his name and pseudonym. Witness DD/1, the usher will show you a piece of paper with your name on it. Please tell us whether that is indeed your name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interpreters are telling me that they are not hearing the witness very well. Mr. Deretic, let us begin, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Mr. Deretic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/1, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as this is a protected witness, could we please briefly go into private session for some identification information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session. Please continue, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the beginning of the war in the area of Prijedor municipality and in Bosnia-Herzegovina as a whole, where were you residing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: In Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when power was taken over in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: On the 30th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who took over power?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: The Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall how this takeover evolved? Did it happen by peaceful means or by force of arms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: By peaceful means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when Prijedor was attacked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: On the 30th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who it was that attacked Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the attack on Prijedor, were there any casualties, any dead soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the attack on Prijedor, where were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: At home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Make a short pause for the interpretation, please. Where was your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, has the witness got any notes in front of him?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see any from here, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please proceed. Because I see whenever he's giving his answer, the witness is looking at the monitor rather than at you. It's simply to make sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/1, where is Puharska? Is it in the centre of town, on the outskirts? In which town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: It is in the outskirts of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the ethnic composition of the inhabitants of the Puharska district was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: There were more Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please give us your answer now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. There were more Muslims, but there were also Serbs and Croats. But the Muslims were the majority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, is your house today in Puharska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: It was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who destroyed your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: The Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Prijedor was attacked, and you said this happened on the 30th of May --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- did you personally suffer any consequences as a result of that attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of consequences?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: We were collected and taken to a camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who rounded you up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: The army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did this happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: On the 30th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this in the morning or in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: About midday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At about what time did this happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: At about 12.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please describe this event to Their Honours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So tell us, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: The soldiers came in our part of Puharska and said all of us under 60 had to come out onto the road. We all went to the road --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just slow down a little.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: We were lined up against a fence. We were all standing there with our hands raised. The soldiers came, they beat us and mistreated us, and they boarded us onto buses and drove us off to Omarska. In Omarska I didn't stay for more than two hours, and then I was taken back to Keraterm. This applies to both me and my brothers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told by those soldiers why you were being rounded up and taken there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: They told us that we were going there for interrogation, to see whether we had taken part in the attack on Prijedor or whether we had been involved in that attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were first taken to Omarska.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the place you were taken to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: There were mostly Muslims detained there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this a kind of compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it fenced in, this compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you stay there for only two hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Because there was no more room for us there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you went back to Keraterm --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- did you all get off?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: We did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you known a person by the name of Zoran Zigic up till then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet that person in Keraterm then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I met Zigic two or three days after my arrival there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you or, rather, do you remember the occasion when you first came into contact with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I do. There was a shortage of cigarettes in the camp at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just please slow down.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: So there were no cigarettes. I saw a soldier smoking, and I asked him, "Could I have a cigarette?" and that is how I came to meet Zoran Zigic. Zoran Zigic gave me a cigarette, and I thanked him for it. Then Zoran Zigic asked me --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: He asked me, "Would you sell some cigarettes?" and I said I would. So I sold some, and Zoran Zigic left me two packages of Kent cigarettes, and that is how I came to meet him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Zoran Zigic in any way hurt you physically or mentally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that time period when you met him, did he give you any kind of assistance in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did he assist you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: He saved my life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to explain what exactly you mean when you say he saved your life.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I will. I was in the camp. A soldier came up to me. He took out a knife to kill me. I ran to Zoran Zigic and said, "Look, Zigic. This one wants to kill me." And then Zigic said to me, "Sit down there. Not a hair may be touched on your head." So I sat down there, and I had something to eat and to drink together with Zoran Zigic, and Zigic accompanied me to the dormitory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Zigic armed on that occasion? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that first encounter you had with Zoran Zigic, do you remember how he was dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: He was wearing a camouflage uniform and a red beret.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you perhaps remember any other details that were characteristic of Zoran Zigic at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: His left hand was bandaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw Zoran Zigic for the first time and then the days that followed, did you see him again; if you did, and when was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: In the first half of the month of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you see him every day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to his left bandaged hand, did you notice that at any time he had dyed hair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you met him for the first time, what colour was his hair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Black.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice Zoran Zigic wearing any earrings, one or two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever notice that he may have been wearing black gloves with the fingers cut off?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at Keraterm --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- could you tell us where you were put up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: In number 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean "number 2"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Room 2, where we were put up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many rooms were there at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at Keraterm, how many rooms were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after you were put up in this room, were you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times were you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many days after you arrived in Keraterm were you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Three or four days after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us: After you arrived and when you were interrogated, what were you interrogated about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I was asked whether I had participated in the attack on Prijedor and whether I had engaged in any black marketeering with weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the interrogation, did your status change in Keraterm itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: It did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how did it change?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I was transferred to Room 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you given any duties then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were your duties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I was put in charge of food and water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you expected to do with the food and water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: To carry food and water and to distribute it, because in the morning, when we had breakfast, we would all line up, and as I was charged with the duty of distributing the food, some people would take five times and some wouldn't get to have one helping.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your freedom of movement restricted after the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, in connection with what you just said: Did anyone assist you in the distribution of food and water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The name, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the food and water came from to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I just know about the water. I don't know about the food. The water came from a tank truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where it was brought from, the water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: From the utilities company water supply system, in tank trucks, the first time. And then I went with Zoran Zigic to fetch water also in a minibus. I went, and my brothers, with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what Zoran Zigic was doing in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you mentioned the minibus, did you see Zoran drive it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see what he was transporting in the minibus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that at first you were accommodated in Room 2, and after that, after the interrogation, in Room 1; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, about your brothers. After you arrived in Keraterm, which room were they put into?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Room 2, until the interrogation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: In Room 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the day, were you able to move around inside the compound of the Keraterm facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while you were walking around, did you see Zoran Zigic inside the compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Only once. Only when Sead Jusufagic was brought in in a police van.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell us, please: In Room 2, where you were accommodated --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- can you tell us what size this room was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I know it was a big room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of door was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: It was a metal door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were moved to Room 1, what kind of door was there on that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: It was -- there were bars, so that you could see through them. You could see everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell me, please: Were you able to move around the Keraterm compound by night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On those occasions, did you see Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with your permission, I will ask for the assistance of the usher. I have in front of me a sketch of Keraterm. I think it comes from my colleagues in the OTP, and we have copied it in several copies. So I would like to have it shown to the witness so that he can explain to the Chamber where each room was and whether this is a sketch of Keraterm, because I will be asking questions about certain details, so it will be easier for the Trial Chamber to follow. Would you be so kind as to distribute this. Would you put a copy on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, does this exhibit already have a number or is this the first time we see it? I think it's the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. This is the first time I am showing this sketch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, what number will it have?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... E8/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. With your permission, I will continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The transcript is not clear. Could you switch on your microphone and start speaking only once it is lit. What is exhibit number, Madam Registrar, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The exhibit number is D8/4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, but isn't it Exhibit D4/8 because we have the accused number 4? Isn't that so, Madam Registrar? This is the fourth accused.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Right, Your Honour, and that's why the "4" is after the number of exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I don't think so. What was the system used for the other Defence counsel, Madam Registrar, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: A number was given and then a slash and then the number of the accused. So I'm following the same order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, then. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/1, you see this sketch in front of you. Is this the sketch of the Keraterm investigation centre in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter could not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show us where Room 1 was and Room 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please write it in in pencil and have it marked -- mark it "X" or "1" and "2". And in front of Room 1, could you write the number "1".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure that you have marked these rooms correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please indicate where the toilet was in this room. If there was one, of course.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Between 3 and 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This sketch can be taken off the ELMO now, and, Mr. President, I will go on with my questions, but we are sure to need the sketch for future reference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/1, did you know a person named Sead Jusufagic, nicknamed Car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that person before your arrival in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he brought to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of person was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: You mean Car?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. What was Car like as a person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, he was a thief. He did time in gaols. He was tried. I knew him before the war, and he used to steal and commit burglaries, and he spent time in prisons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember when Car was brought to Keraterm? For example, in comparison to your arrival.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, it was two or three days after I arrived in Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember how Car was brought to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Car was brought in in a police van, number 53.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that number mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, that refers to a machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where he was brought from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: From the hill. From Brdo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by "Brdo"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, it's the vicinity of Prijedor, because that was where fighting going on and that's where he was caught. It's near Prijedor, near Rizvanovici, Bircani, Zecovi, Carakovo, Hambarine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are those villages? Are you telling us the names of villages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Car was brought to Keraterm, did you see him there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Car maltreated in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who beat him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, the first time he came in -- when he was brought in in the police van, I saw soldiers around him, and they made him run around in circles with the 53 machine-gun, and I saw soldiers beating him in the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any of the soldiers --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- and reserve policemen --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- who were beating Sead Jusufagic, also known as Car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. I knew only Cupo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you slow down, please. Whom did you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Cupo Banovic. I don't know what his name was, his first name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the way in which the soldiers and policemen beat Car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, it was because they had caught him with the light machine-gun, the 53.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But how did they beat him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, they kicked him. They punched him. Cupo hit him with a truncheon, in fact, with a baseball bat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe his appearance? What did he look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. He was thin, yellow -- of a sallow complexion. His teeth were missing. He had long fair hair. I know Sead very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell me, please --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Car running around the compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Only once, when he was brought in in the police van.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who made him run round the compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: The group of soldiers and reserve policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us, please, did you see Zoran Zigic among that group of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Zoran Zigic beat Car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: He only kicked him once, from behind, in the bottom, because I was there and I saw it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far were you from that group of soldiers and from Car when he was running?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, about 10 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to ask for the usher's assistance again and to put back the sketch on the ELMO. I will need it for my next question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember --

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have this. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, could you please point with your pencil to the place where Car was running, how he was running, in what direction, and how this happened, whether Car was running from Room 1 to Room 4, over the entire area, or was it somewhere else. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to indicate with your pencil where Car was running and how he was running.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, he was running in circles like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he running in only one direction or in a circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: He was running in a circle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show it to us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, perhaps instructions should be given to the witness for him to point out to us on the ELMO so that we can see that, and the witness probably doesn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I meant. Could the usher assist?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In front of which room was he running?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: In front of number 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, where did you mark number 1? Could you show us now where he was running?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while he was running -- could you now put the letter "C" in the middle of this circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, does this mean that this is the circle in which Car was running?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the breadth of that circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't very big.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what was the diameter? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, it was about 5 metres long and 4 metres wide. It was a small circle where he was running.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, where the soldiers were as Car was running?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: They were standing around him. Car was in the middle and the soldiers were standing all around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times did you see him run the circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And apart from this running, apart from this incident when you said the soldiers were beating him, did you see Car being beaten later on by soldiers or policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And among the soldiers who were beating Car, did you see Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. I only saw him once. I only saw him kick Car in the bottom on one occasion, just after he had been brought in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when Car died?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did this happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: From the 6th to the 7th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he beaten then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who beat him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, the soldiers called out his name when Zoran Karlica was killed. After they returned to Keraterm from his funeral, they called out for Car. They called out his name there at night and they beat him. I heard his screams. You could hear everything. And they beat him there. It was Nikica Janjic, Mica Banovic and Cupo Banovic who beat him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain who Zoran Karlica was? Could you just pause for the interpretation, please. So who was Zoran Karlica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, Zoran Karlica was a Major in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he from Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember -- this group of soldiers who came back from the funeral, do you remember what time it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, it was after midnight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did they beat Car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Near Room 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the Keraterm compound lighted up at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. There were two lampposts only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that night, did you see Car dead?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: In the morning, when with I came out of Room 1. A soldier came to fetch me and ordered me to carry him to Room 4, behind the pallets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of pallets were these?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: They were the Keraterm factory pallets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they made of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Wood. Wooden boards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/1, apart from the time when you saw Zigic kick Car that you described, did you see on any other occasion that Zoran beat Car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. It was only what I described. When Car was brought in in a police van, Zoran Zigic hit him only once. In fact, he kicked him in the bottom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a person called Emsud Bahonjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a person called Drago Tokmadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: A policeman before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was Drago Tokmadzic brought to Keraterm? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Between the 8th and the 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between the 8th and the 10th? What month? Was it the same month when Car was brought in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many days after you were brought in was Drago Tokmadzic brought in? Can you tell us what month it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember the month. I know approximately the day. It was six or seven days after I was brought in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. After Drago Tokmadzic was brought to Keraterm, what room was he brought to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Number 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Drago Tokmadzic moved from this room during his stay in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see Drago Tokmadzic beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Drago Tokmadzic dead?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you see him when he was dead?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: In front of Room 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Drago Tokmadzic wearing or what did he have on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: A police uniform and a police cap with a five-pointed star.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember when he was brought in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he wearing then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: A police uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he wearing a cap at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, with a five-pointed star.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell me, please, when you saw Drago Tokmadzic dead, can you tell us approximately when that might have been?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, it was on the 26th of July [as interpreted] that I saw Drago dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say the 20th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. I meant the 20th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't hear you properly. You said that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: The interpretation that I heard was the 26th, but then after that, Mr. Deretic repeated the date as the 20th and the transcript has changed. Maybe we can check to see whether it is the 26th or the 20th. My objection was that Mr. Deretic was leading after the witness gave that answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the date in the LiveNote is the 20th of June, but in any event, you heard the objection. So, Mr. Deretic, do you have a reply?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I heard the witness use the word "July," so I just wanted the witness to repeat. He said "June," in fact - I misheard - and we see "June" in the transcript. So the witness said the 26th -- the 20th of June. Mr. President, to avoid and exclude any vagueness, let me ask the witness once again does he remember --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Put the question to the witness once more.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember when you saw Drago Tokmadzic dead?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: On the 20th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the 20th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that is the date in the LiveNote, page 26, line 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I think it's clear now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/1, you said that you didn't see when Drago Tokmadzic was killed. Do you know what he died of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: He died from the beatings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I saw it when I carried him. I saw blood trickling from his mouth, from the head. It wasn't the result of a pistol shot or a gunshot but from blows. There was blood that had thickened on his head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any haematoma, swellings on Drago Tokmadzic's body, that is, bruises?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you carried Drago Tokmadzic. Why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I was ordered to carry him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave you that order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: A soldier. I don't remember his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to who beat Drago Tokmadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you saw him on the 20th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, a couple of days before that day, and after that day, did you see Zoran Zigic in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your stay in the Keraterm investigation centre, could you tell us when you found it most difficult?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The night of the 24th to the 25th. That was the worst.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't mention the month. You just gave the dates.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: The month of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the same month as the one when you saw Drago Tokmadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you perhaps be more precise as to the period that passed from the moment you arrived until this date that you mentioned? How long into your stay was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: How long?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: Could you remember how much time went by from the moment you arrived until this event that you just mentioned? Did it happen in the same month in which you arrived or several months later? Could you tell us something more about the time that elapsed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, I can't. I don't know. It was a long time ago. It was nine years ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, I know I heard a moan in Room 3. They were moaning. I heard shooting. I heard shooting and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember, was that during the day or during the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: After midnight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that day, that is, the day before night fell, what kind of day was it? Was it a sunny day, a rainy day? Was it overcast?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: It was a sunny day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you or someone else distributed food to the detainees that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. I did, and [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember whether it was breakfast, lunch, or dinner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Breakfast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About what time was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: About 11.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember to which room you distributed the food?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: To the persons in number 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the customary time for distributing food in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you distribute water to the detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who distributed the water with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Myself and [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe how you gave water to the detainees or, rather, where they were at the time. Were they outside or in the rooms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: In Room 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you carry the water in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: In plastic bottles of one and a half litres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that room locked or unlocked at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: It was locked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of a door did Room 3 have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: A metal door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how would you pass the water to the detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: [redacted] was responsible for us. He would unlock the door and I gave them bottles with the water to drink.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in the Keraterm compound in the afternoon too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Zoran Zigic at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, were you able to intimate or to have any feeling of foreboding about something that was going to happen that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything at all that was unusual occur in Keraterm on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, it did not. Everything was normal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us who were the persons who were detained in Room 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I can. They were people from Kozarac and from Brdo. They were in Room 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to why those persons from those particular villages were in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Because there was a war going on in Kozarac and in Brdo. There was fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/1, can you recall when those persons were brought to Room 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know or do you remember that those persons may have been brought in that day or earlier on --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- in relation to the shooting you mention?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: The witness said that he cannot remember when they were brought to the camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in answer to my question, the witness said that he did not remember on what day they were brought in, so I'm reminding him of the shooting so that perhaps that would refresh his memory in relation to the shooting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Waidyaratne. They are two different questions, so Mr. Deretic is quite in order in posing his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's one thing to know whether the witness knows the date, and another question is whether the persons were brought in, so these are two quite different matters. Continue, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember that day and whether there were any weapons positioned within the Keraterm compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of weapons were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Rifles 53 and other rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is a 53? Is that a machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, a light machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many such light machine-guns were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recollect where they were positioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could I ask the usher for his assistance once again, if he could assist the witness, please, so that the witness can show the positions of those machine-guns. So could you please be at the side of the witness to speed things up and assist him when necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to show us or, rather, to mark with an "X" the positions of those machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: There was one here and there was another one here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what those machine-guns were positioned on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: They were placed on the ground. There were some defences around them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the defence consist of, the shield?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Sand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether there were any sacks there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. They were sacks with gravel and sand inside, sandbags, in other words.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you heard the shooting after midnight.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you during the shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: In Room 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your brothers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Also in Room 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the room with the bars on the doors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Trial Chamber what you were able to see from that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I could see the compound and right up to the scales, the weighing machine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said "the weighing machine." Could you show us on the sketch where that machine was? Could you show us on the ELMO? Can you see it on this sketch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: This is where the weighing device was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... my learned friend, but to assist the Court, because the machine-guns had been marked with the sign "X" and also the weighing machine with the sign "X," it could be differentiated by some other letter. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're quite right. I thought it was a "Y," actually, perhaps a plus or a "Y." I don't know whether the witness is able to do that. In any event, there should be a clear distinction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe you could put "X1" there. Witness, do you remember whether there was a hut next to that weighing machine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recollect whether the Keraterm compound was lit that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: They were only two lampposts that were working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean pillars with a lamp on top?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many were there within the Keraterm compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: There were four or five, but only two were functioning and the light was poor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that evening, can you remember when the shooting started?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: After midnight, and it was with interruptions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recollect whether the light was later intensified in the Keraterm compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. A generator with floodlights arrived, and I know that this floodlight had a stand, and it was placed there close to Room 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So before that floodlight was positioned, had the shooting already started? Did you hear moans or screams? Did you see anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I did. We heard screams.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you watching from Room 1 what was going on in the compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I couldn't see Room 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were you looking out into the compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. I could see the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see the machine-guns from your room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the machine-gun from which fire was opened on Room 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Because I couldn't see the machine-gun shooting, but I did see the machine-gun. It was next to hut 1, and it was close to Room 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see it from your room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anyone in the compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there soldiers in the compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, they were, but they had all gone to -- towards Room 3, and there was a guard at the gates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them move?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: You mean the soldiers? Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice Zoran Zigic then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, I did not, because I was able to walk around during the day and during the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did this shooting go on for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: For about two or three hours, with breaks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave your room in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time could that have been?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Around 6.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your room locked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who unlocked the room? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you left your room, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I saw a lot of bodies and wounded people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, excuse me for interrupting you. How much more time, roughly, do you need to complete your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we've been working for an hour and a half. Another hour, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. I think it's time for a break. So we're now going to have a half-hour break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Witness DD/1, are you comfortable?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you can see, Judge Fouad Riad has joined us. We knew yesterday that he wouldn't be here at the beginning. Just to let you know that he's with us now. Mr. Deretic, there appears to be a problem with the sketch, the model.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence of Mr. Zigic found during the break that the sketch we presented is really not good enough. The Witness B [as interpreted], who was a direct participant in everything that happened in Keraterm, he was there, so we think that during his testimony we should have a model of Keraterm here so that he can present to the Court all the facts he has been questioned about, and especially the facts that I intend to question him about now. For example, just to clarify this a bit, one of my questions was that the witness should say whether he saw the weigh hut. The witness marked a building here and said what he did, that the scales should be around here. But if shown a model, he would certainly be able to clarify all the remaining questions about the position of the scales, of the machine-guns, of the place where Car had to run in circles, and so on and so forth, and some of these things cannot be seen here on this sketch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. A remark of a general nature first. I think for things to flow properly, you need to communicate well with the Chamber. The question raised by Mr. Stojanovic before we began is a good example of this. Ms. Kate Mackintosh is the legal officer of the Chamber for this case - you see her here - and whenever you have a problem with the Chamber, contact Ms. Kate Mackintosh, even if you think that it is a question that need not be raised. In this way, things can be organised and clarified so that we can function well. And this also applies equally to the Defence and to the Prosecution. This is something that you should have availed yourself of, that is, the assistance of Ms. Kate Mackintosh. Even if you fear that the question may be a stupid one, put it to Ms. Kate Mackintosh. After that, we will see. So the problem we have is the following: A model, as you know, is not something we can put in our pockets, so though many people are working here, this has to be organised, because the model is guarded; it needs to be carried in because it's heavy. So we can't provide it immediately. So what I think we should do is the following: You continue with your examination-in-chief with the instruments and tools that you have available now. Then we will have a lunch break. You have already told us that you need more or less an hour to finish. Yes, an hour and a quarter maybe. Then we will reach the time of the lunch break. During the lunch break, the model will be assembled, but as you know, it doesn't have legs of its own, so it has to be carried in. And after that, either you will have questions to clarify, with the help of the model, and you will do so, or you may not have other questions and we can begin with the cross-examination. But I would like to hear the Prosecutor regarding this proposition of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. In fact, I was thinking I was not going to use the model, but I was going to use another photograph of the Keraterm camp which we have already admitted into evidence. If I may say the number, it's 3/27. So even if the model is not there, the Prosecution would be able to ask questions pertaining to the evidence with regard to this witness through another photograph. I also state, Your Honour, that as the Keraterm case, the case is proceeding in Courtroom I. The model may be there. That's subject to correction, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you very much for your suggestion, but I think that it is up to the Defence counsel to present the testimony as it wishes, and I think working with the photograph is a way of having something tendered into evidence. But if you have a model, it is easier to indicate things and this is registered Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. in the transcript. We should have all the models here of the camps, because, after all, they are tools that we need to use, but we have to use them well. Mr. Deretic, have you any response to Mr. Waidyaratne's suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We agree absolutely with everything you have said. Evidently, we overestimated our witness's abilities, because we thought the sketch would be quite sufficient for him to answer with precision the questions put to him. However, this was evidently not the case. We regret this, but now we feel, for the sake of the Trial Chamber and our learned friends, it would be necessary to have the model brought in here so that the witness, who was an eyewitness to all this, can answer all the questions I put to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but Mr. Deretic, you have to count on another difficulty. Because this witness is a protected witness, with facial distortion, it's rather difficult for him to get up and point at the model because he might thereby disclose his identity, or we could always go into closed session for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, precisely so. We have thought about this, and we will ask for a closed session in that part of our examination. I said that I would need an hour, but I think it will be a little less. In that way, we can make up for the time lost to do with the model.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw Mr. Waidyaratne, who was about to get on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just for a clarification. If I understood you correctly, Mr. Deretic will complete his examination after the model is brought. Then thereafter, I will be permitted to cross-examine. Is that the position? Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not necessarily, Mr. Waidyaratne, because once we have the model in the courtroom, Mr. Deretic may need additional explanations with the help of the model. So in any event, you will cross-examine after the lunch break. That is certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, we must proceed, otherwise, this will go on forever.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite so, Mr. President. Thank you very much. I will have only a few questions to put with the model here, and I will be very quick about it. If you will permit me, I will now continue examining the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/1, when you left your room in the morning, you said this was at about 6.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see a truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of truck was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: It was from Autotransport. It was a big truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by "Autotransport"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, that was a company called Autotransport in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you know that the truck was from Autotransport?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Because there was lettering on the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show exactly where you saw this truck in the Keraterm compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: In front of Room 3. It came in backwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was someone standing in front of the truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the driver of the truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the driver wearing a military uniform or civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if possible, I would like to ask for us to go into closed session again because of the next several questions I have to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let us go into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may continue, Mr. Deretic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you be so kind and explain, illustrate as clearly as you can, how many bodies you saw, how many - if you know, of course - you loaded onto the truck, whether there were wounded people among them, what happened to them, whether anyone provided any kind of assistance to them, and so on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: All I know is that there were a lot of wounded people and a lot of dead people, and with my own hands, I loaded the wounded and the dead onto the truck. From that day on, I couldn't bear to eat with my hands. My brother put food in my mouth because I was covered with blood and there was blood running down my arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where this truck was taken to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that truck driven away by the same person who was standing next to the truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. It was the driver, in civilian clothes, who came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please, because almost eight or nine years have elapsed in the meantime, can you recall how long the loading of these people who are, unfortunately, dead, lasted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: About an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/1, I would now like to take you back to the time when you heard the gunfire at night. On that occasion, while the shooting was going on, did you hear from any one of the people in the Rooms 1, 2, or 3? Did you hear anyone mention Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please: Do you remember whether the truck returned to the Keraterm compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that on the same day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember what time it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: In the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened next to the truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell us, please, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: The soldiers ordered my brother to wash the truck and scrub it with a brush, and the truck was full of blood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did this take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, about an hour, an hour and a quarter, about an hour and 15 minutes, because it was being scrubbed with a brush. The blood had become dry and it was caked in blood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to the truck afterwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: The truck was driven away somewhere. I don't know where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/1, until when were you in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Until mid-August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this, were you taken somewhere or were you released?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I was transferred to the Trnopolje camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And until the time you were transferred to Trnopolje, but after this event, did you ever see Zoran Zigic in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. As I said, I saw him in mid-July and then I didn't see him any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to repeat when you left Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: In mid-August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me: How long was this after this event that you have just described in Keraterm, after the massacre in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you spend in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Fifteen days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see Zoran Zigic there at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one more question about this topic. During your stay in Keraterm, did you ever see Zoran Zigic beating people up or killing someone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. I was always in the compound. I could wander around at will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
