utterances.text: Did you see any excesses committed by him, apart from the incident with Car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know about the contents of an article published in Euroblic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. I've read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: On the 21st.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it last week?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does this article refer to the trial of Dusko Sikirica, Damir Dosen, and Dragan Kolundzija before this Tribunal? Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, you said that you had read the article.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The article mentions Witness A, a Muslim from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. Now the counsel is giving evidence. He's referring to the article. He's saying the article refers to A, Witness A. I don't know who it is, which this is article is, and the witness has already said he remembers -- he knows about an article. He says that he didn't know anything about that article, so which I think my learned friend should not proceed with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, unfortunately I have only been here for five months, and during that time I have been reading the transcripts and applying the same methods as the Prosecution. They have shown to witnesses articles which the witnesses had never read, and I have here with me last Wednesday's newspaper, and I know the witness has read them, and I just wanted to ask him, within the context of the question so far, a few questions, for the sake of clarification, if I may, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, has the Prosecutor got that article? Mr. Waidyaratne?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He must have a copy and so must we, even though we need not read everything. Something else: If the witness has told you that he doesn't remember the article, he has read it but he doesn't remember it, then the next step would be to show it to the witness to remind him; otherwise there's no point in asking him questions when he said that he doesn't remember. So that is the objection of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness said -- he didn't say that he cannot remember the article. The witness said that he doesn't remember mention being made of Sikirica, Dosen, and Kolundzija, but the witness said that he had read the article. I would be much more specific than I have been so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Please go ahead, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the witness that was mentioned under his pseudonym said in that article that Zoran Zigic forced Car to run around the compound, after which he beat him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. Zoran Zigic did not force him to run around the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also in that article, it says --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to this line of questioning. Still I don't know what from Mr. Deretic is quoting or as to who this witness is. He's referring to some -- his question is: "So the witness that was mentioned under his pseudonym ..." We don't know as to who this witness is, as to from where this is taken, and as to whether this witness knows anything about this matter. It's not clear from the question, Your Honour, if you see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Has the Prosecution got a copy of that article? I think you already told me that they do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we don't know who that person is. We just know the person from the pseudonym appearing in the article. It's an article appearing last Wednesday, and we got hold of it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but have you provided the Prosecution with a copy of that article?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps that might be important, to provide them with an article.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Is it in English or B/C/S? That's all. You must know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Serbian. I have the original newspaper, in the original. It was issued last Wednesday. And of course, we are ready to provide the Chamber and the Prosecution with copies and even to tender it into evidence. Mr. President, may I be allowed to show the witness this article and allow him to read it and to answer a few points that were touched upon during the day? It's nothing new. Because we are trying to prove in this way what actually happened in Keraterm and the kinds of reports that are appearing in the media. We're just asking whether the allegations contained in the article are true or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a minute. We'll see. Mr. Waidyaratne, do you need the article?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all, now I will base my objection on a different way. Mr. Deretic is trying to -- in fact, the question and answer was -- now it's not on the screen. He's asking this witness to comment about a witness who has given evidence in another case and which is reported in these papers, as to whether it's true or not, and which, I think, during the Prosecution case, which was resolved, saying that we should not refer to other witnesses' evidence and ask them for any opinion as to whether it was true or not. If I'm correct, Your Honour, I would give you the line and the time. It's at page 47, and it says: "Does this article refer to the trial of Dusko Sikirica, Damir Dosen, Kolundzija before the Tribunal? Can you remember?" Further down it says, page 49, line 2: "So the witness that was mentioned under his pseudonym said in that article that Zoran Zigic forced Car to run around the compound, after which he beat him; is that correct?" Answer: "No. Zoran Zigic did not force him to run around the compound." He's quoting some evidence from another trial and he's asking this witness to comment on that. That's my objection too. Thank you, Your Honour. And we would like to have the article too, if a copy could be given to us. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the copy that you would like to have, Mr. Waidyaratne, do you want it now or after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: After the break, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So during the break. Mr. Deretic, you understand now the objection of the Prosecution. We are not here to make a confrontation between two different witnesses. As we do in our system, when one witness says one thing and another, another, we bring both and confront them. That is not what we do here. You have a witness here and you have to put the question to him, and then the Chamber will assess the value of one witness and the value of another. You are not able to confront the two. Do you understand that? Please proceed. I think Judge Wald has a comment to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I just want to register my disagreement, I think, with that. It seems to me that you can ask a question based upon an article in a newspaper. If it just said, "It has been reported that a witness, you know, said such-and-such," I think that it's, at least in my view, valid to ask the person, "There has been a report in the newspaper that Zigic made Car run around in a circle. Is that in accord with your observation?" And the witness can then answer according to his observation. I don't see that you can have a system whereby you're not ever allowed to refer to a different version simply because the different version may have emanated from a former trial. But I simply want to register my view. It seems to me, Mr. Deretic, you can ask the question, actually get around this by asking it, you know, directly again: In your observation, did Car -- was Car forced to run around the Tribunal and get away from all this -- or run around the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We are not in disagreement, nevertheless. I think that you mustn't ask the witness whether that other witness is right or not, but you should say, "That witness said such-and-such. What is your version?" That is the way you should put the question. "What is the truth, according to you?" But not challenge the other witness: "Did he lie? Did he tell the truth?" So actually, we are fully in agreement. You can use that information on the same basis that a counsel is allowed to say, "I assume that. Am I right?"? So it's something like that. I have this information from the newspaper and what is true, rather than asking whether that other witness told the truth or not. So I think we quite agree. So please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I had no intention to comment on the article, as my learned friend has said. I just wanted to put a question to the witness in that connection, and I'll do so now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The article report says literally that: "Zoran Zigic forced Car, carrying a heavy machine-gun over his shoulder, to run in a circle while a certain Duca hit him with a truncheon which had a metal ball attached to it at the end."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Zoran Zigic did not force him to run in a circle. I can assert that with certainty. It wasn't Zoran Zigic who forced him but a group of soldiers and a group of regular policemen. When they caught him up there at Brdo, they forced him to run around immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Dusko Knezevic, known as Duca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he the person who had this truncheon with a metal ball on the end of it on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two more questions if I may, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The article goes on to say that: "Zigic, after that, took a bottle of mineral water of one litre and ordered Car to take off his pants and to sit on the bottle, and Zigic was forcing him onto the bottle."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you comment on this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I can. I know that that is not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far away were you from the site, from the spot where the event occurred? Though I think I've already asked you when I asked you about Car running around in a circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I was about 15 metres away. So I saw it all. I saw everything. I was there in the compound. I was outside when Car was brought in in a police van.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One more question. Witness A recounted that he watched as, in July 1992, soldiers mounted two machine-guns on school desks in front of the room in which men were locked in from a part of the Prijedor municipality of Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I object to this question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: On what basis? I don't know whether my learned friend is referring to the article again or the witness who has given evidence in another trial, because this witness's question was it was not so, it was not. It was on the ground and there were sandbags.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could my learned friend hear me out first, please. I haven't finished. Could you wait for the question and then object. I haven't finished. You don't know what I'm going to ask before I've finished reading the quotation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Deretic has just told you that he's quoting from an article, after which he will ask his question. But perhaps you should make it quite clear where you begin the quote and where you end the quote.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the quote begins now: "The Witness A recounted that he watched as, in July 1992, soldiers mounted two machine-guns on school desks in front of the room in which men were locked in who came from a part of the Prijedor municipality called Brdo. The detainees were not given food or water."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my first question to you, Witness, is: Were the machine-guns mounted on school desks and were there any school desks there anyway?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. The machine-guns were not placed on school desks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my second question: Were the detainees given food or not, as you have already told us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: They were. I gave them food and water. I was in charge of both food and water.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And finally, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Deretic. Witness DD/1, you said the machine-guns were not placed on school desks. Where were they placed, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: One was facing towards the Banja Luka road that I have shown, and another one was between number 3. I know that it was put there because I saw it there and I was right next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On what? On what? On what was it placed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: There was a shield with sandbags, and it was placed on that pile of sandbags.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/1, why have you decided to testify for Zoran Zigic in The Hague Tribunal, a person who has been suspected of war crimes against civilians, in view of everything that you have lived through and in view of your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Because Zoran Zigic helped me. Had it not been for him, I would be in the ground, both myself and my brothers. I know that Zoran never said anything offensive to me or my brothers. He gave me food. He never hit me. It never even occurred to him to hit me. And I was in charge of food and water. I too was beaten. I too am a victim. They would beat me sometimes for three hours at night. You wouldn't even know who was doing it. They put me in a barrel that was full of water. My head was under the water and my legs on top.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this happen in the presence of Zoran?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. When Zoran Zigic was there, it never happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you very much. I have no more questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Deretic. So I think this is a good time for our lunch break. The Registry will take care of the model, and if Mr. Deretic has a few more additional questions with the model, then he will do so. And I think that Mr. Deretic will make copies of this article and provide them to the Prosecution. So we're now going to have a 50-minute lunch break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Mr. Deretic, where are we now in relation to what we granted you?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, unfortunately, for technical reasons, or at least that's what we have been told, the technical personnel were unable to bring in the model, and I think that the Prosecution does not object to this, because it is their exhibit. So we still would insist on this, however, if there is a technical possibility of at least bringing it in tomorrow morning before the start of the session, since we have another witness tomorrow who could also testify to the same circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. Go ahead, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have just finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are telling me that you don't need it for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, technically it is not possible to have the model here now, so there would be no point in insisting on it. We don't know how to solve this technically, and time is running. That's why I said this. We would like to have this witness testify about those circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Deretic mentioned the non-objection on the part of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do not object to the question whether the model could be brought to Court and he could be examined, but may I respectfully say to Your Honours that I would be cross-examining the witness with regard to his ability to show certain places that he has faltered in certain areas I'm going to cross-examine. So therefore, I don't think Mr. Deretic will be -- will have an opportunity to re-examine him with regard to that, will have an opportunity to re-examine, but I would cross-examine with regard to the certain places that he has shown and what he has pointed out in the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is quite clear to the Defence counsel of Mr. Zigic. However, it would be much more useful if we had the model here now, while my learned friend is cross-examining the witness about these circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But in any event, Mr. Deretic, it seems to me that you will always have a chance during your re-examination to get additional information. But we shall continue with the cross-examination of this witness by the Prosecution. I think it is Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. Your Honour, may I be permitted to go into a brief private session, as I would be asking certain questions which may affect his identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that we are in public session. You may continue, Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the day that you were arrested, do you remember that day when the Serb soldiers came to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the date, and which month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Oh, dear. A long time has passed. I can't remember the date. I know that we were taken away on the 30th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you taken to Jove Djukice Street in Donja Puharska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please don't mention any of the names of your brothers if you answer the questions, but you can answer. Where were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: To the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you were taken to the Omarska camp, the Serb soldiers asked you, your other brothers, two brothers, to go to a certain gathering point in the Jove Djukice Street; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you put into the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: [redacted], in front of our house, because there were quite a lot of us and there were a number of buses, and they blindfolded -- or rather, we had to keep our eyes closed and our heads down so that we wouldn't see where they were driving us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you beaten when you were getting into the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With what, and who beat you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, the soldiers. I don't know their names. It was the soldiers who came from Pakrac. And you can still see scars on my chin. That's how they beat me. That was when they rounded us up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that from there you were taken to Omarska and for around two hours you were in Omarska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The two brothers of yours were with you in the bus when you were in Omarska; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in Omarska, did you see any detainees of Muslim ethnicity in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, I saw them in Omarska, in the compound, lying down or sitting down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then from Omarska you were brought to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you searched and beaten when you were brought to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. I was beaten only once on the bus and when we were rounded up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you searched when you got down from the bus at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that time, were you beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Not me. I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the others beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, others were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, did you know Keraterm well before you went there? Have you seen Keraterm, this place that you were taken to, before this instance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, but I never entered the compound before. I would pass by on my way to Banja Luka by car and I would see it. I didn't know that this was Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I may say, it's on the Banja Luka-Prijedor main road; you could see it from the main road, this place which you call Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anybody who was going on the road could see that clearly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said in your direct examination you were sent to Room 1; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or were you sent to Room 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. No. First I was in Room 2, up to my questioning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: After that, in Room 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your position is: When you arrived, you were sent to Room 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it Room 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the questioning, you were sent to Room 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: After the questioning, I was sent to number 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were your brothers, two brothers, with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, they were, up to the questioning. When they were questioned, then they were sent to number 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they questioned at the same time that you were questioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. I was the last one to be questioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they questioned on the same date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they were more or less with you in Room 1 and Room 2; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, when you were in Room 2, did you see Car, the person by the name Car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see a person by the name of Emsud Bahonjic in Room 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see a person by the name of Samir Sistek?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: There were a lot of people there. I can't remember now. I know that there were a lot of us in that room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Samir Sistek was also nicknamed Coachman, if I may help you. Does that recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because you spoke about Car, I need to ask you this question: When you were in Room 2, did you at any time see the person by the name of Car in the Room 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I was in Room 1 at that time, when Car was brought in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, when Car was brought in, as to where he was kept; in which room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Number 2, and I was in number 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So other than the time that you saw him beaten by the soldiers, and Zoran Zigic once, you didn't see Car when he was in Room 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to clarify, you said that you don't know the person by the name of Emsud Bahonjic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even in camp you didn't see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you said that you were able to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, to the direct question of my learned colleague as to whether he knew Emsud Bahonjic, the witness said he did not know him. After that, the Prosecutor asked whether he saw that man. We object because the witness is -- attempts are being made to confuse the witness. I think that questions should be put quite clearly and unambiguously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: The question is -- I was not trying to mislead the witness, but because he said that he didn't know, I wanted to know as to whether he got to know him subsequently in the camp and whether he knew him after that. That was my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to go to Room 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that time, did you see any persons by the side of the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, there were quite a few of them. I don't know their names now because there were people from everywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Car during that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was in Room 2; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was he seated? Where was he? Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: In the corner. That's where I saw him sitting down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his condition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, he was a bit battered, but only when he first came in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I'm talking about the time that you saw him by the corner. Which corner are you talking about? In the room 2? Which corner? Is it by the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: In the corner, at the bottom. Because I brought water to them and distributed food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The bottom -- in the corner at the bottom. What you mean is to say -- is it right at the end of the room or was it at the entrance of the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, no, no. At the entrance to the room, in the corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other persons injured next to Car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now your question is that you saw Car in Room 2 --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- in the side of the room, at the entrance. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned about the beating of Car by soldiers. Was it the day that you thought that Car was brought to the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. It was when he was brought in a police van.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long after that was he beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, I found him between the 6th and the 7th. I found him dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned the dates 6th and 7th. I'm sorry, Witness, please, from the day you saw him being brought to the camp and you saw him being beaten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After how long after that beating did Car die?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he there for many days in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, not for many days. He succumbed. When they came back from the funeral of Zoran Karlica, I heard them call out his name. They called out --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm sorry to have interrupted you. From the time -- how many days you can count -- say, for instance, was he there for a week?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Three or four days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned about the beating by the soldiers and Zoran Zigic of Car. Where were you when you saw this beating?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, I saw when Car was brought in for the first time in a police van, and I saw that Zoran Zigic only kicked him once in the bottom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when you saw this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: In front of Room 1. They'd let me out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many soldiers -- who were the other soldiers who were there? Did you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, I did, yes. I recognised only Cupo Banovic. I don't know his proper first name. He wore earrings. He had long hair.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Duca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing Duca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Zoran Zigic giving Car a machine-gun to carry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, I didn't, because I know that as soon as Car got out, the soldiers told him to put the machine-gun on his shoulder and run in a circle, because I was standing in the compound, smoking a cigarette, while Car was running in a circle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you see Zoran Zigic give Car the machine-gun to put on his shoulders and run?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that Zigic put the machine-gun on him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anybody asking Car to dismantle the machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anybody asking another person by the name of Emsud, a detainee, to come out and help Car to put the dismantled machine-gun back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Witness, you didn't see -- did you see Car dismantling the machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, because I went to fetch the food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were not there right throughout this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Only when Car was brought in. I was there then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this raining during that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, did you know a person by the name of -- a detainee by the name of Hrdzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: An academic, a professor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. I didn't know him either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, now please tell us a little bit more in detail as to what exactly did the guards ask you. Who asked you to distribute the food?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. [redacted] told me to distribute the food and water, and I was in charge of both the water and the food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what did you give them? Did you see what food was given to these detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was given to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Two pieces of bread. There would be beans, rice, potatoes and that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they ever given more?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you were able to give more to them, you would have given them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I couldn't because some would eat five times and others didn't get a chance to get one helping. We were all hungry. But as much as they gave you, you had to eat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say one person would be able to eat five times. How did that happen? Did you give them -- one person five times? That means ten slices a day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. No. This is how it was: I would distribute the food, and I know a guy who picked up his food once. He went off, ate it, and then lined up again, and he would wait for me to pour the food into his plate again, and I would give it to him. Then the other detainees started cursing me, saying some are eating five times, others don't get a chance to get food once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the guards support you or anybody in that sense?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: [redacted]. He was good to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, [redacted] [redacted]. Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many detainees were there during the time that you spent -- at a given time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: But I know -- there were quite a lot of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't want to press on with the matter, but approximately could you say a number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. I really can't say because I don't know. I know that there were quite a lot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many meals were given to these detainees a day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what time to what time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: From 10.00 to 12.00 and from 2.00 to 4.00. That would be breakfast and lunch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they given this food? Where did you serve them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: In front of Room 2. Here, right here in front of Room 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will come to that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: There was a kitchen there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will come to that. I will show you the photograph later. Do you know who brought the food to the camp? Was it cooked in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: It was cooked in the camp. There were cooks there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know any of those cooks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I don't know. They were elderly women.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said about water and that once you went with Zoran Zigic in the minibus to get water. Do you remember that, in your direct evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go to get the water? How did that come to? Zoran Zigic asked you to get into the bus, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. Zoran Zigic asked whether there were two volunteers, and I volunteered and so did my brother Ismet. And we got into the minibus with Zigic, and we went to fetch the water. We brought it back, unloaded it, and then we went back to our dormitories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go to get the water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I know the man's name was Faruk. I don't know his surname. It's near the new post office in Prijedor. Next to the new post office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what was water brought at that instance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: In jerrycans and in barrels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you with Zoran Zigic in the minibus when you went to get this water in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I spent some time with him, maybe an hour, and an hour and half, because we had to get there and come back, and the water was flowing very slowly and we had to fill the containers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any time did Zoran Zigic ask whether you wanted to go home or whether you should be released? Did you ask him to help in that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. He asked me. He offered to take me home, to have a bath, because there were no bathing facilities. We got lice and all kinds of things over there. And Zoran Zigic did ask me whether I wanted him to take me and my brother home for a bath. I said to Zigic, "Thank you, Zigic, but I don't want to go anywhere from here."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Zoran Zigic able to release any person from the camp? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are sure that he was unable to release any person from the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about it in the camp, that he was able to send people home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, I didn't. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, three times my learned friend is putting the same question to the witness. I really think that is not proper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, if you look closely, you will see that the three questions differ from one another. But perhaps, Mr. Waidyaratne, you could move on a little more quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And whether he knows anything about it, and then you can -- you can ask one-by-one these questions, but please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you. I will do my best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during this time that you spent with Zoran Zigic in the camp and at the time that you went to get -- did you discuss as to what his function in the camp was? Did you ask him as to what he was doing at the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I just asked for a cigarette, to have a smoke, because there were no cigarettes. There was a shortage. One couldn't find cigarettes anywhere. And Zoran Zigic was good to me in the camp. He helped me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask Zoran Zigic at any time as to why you all were detained in this camp and when you were going to be released from this camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that at the -- in your direct examination about Zoran Zigic, meeting Zoran Zigic in the camp, and he, Mr. Zigic, giving you a packet or two of cigarettes to be sold; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times did you do that favour for Mr. Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I went with him for the water, that time, and in Keraterm when he saved my life. Because a man took out a big knife and he wanted to slit my throat, and I ran to Zoran Zigic and I said to him, "Zigic, this one wants to kill me, to slaughter me." And Zigic said, "Don't be afraid. Nobody will hurt you." And then I said to him, "Please, Zigic, take me to my dormitory to lie down," because I didn't dare go alone because this soldier was following me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I don't think you understood the question. Please listen to the question. I asked you about the situation -- the instance where Zoran Zigic gave you a packet of cigarettes or two to be sold. Do you understand that? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I do. I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that time - I will go step by step - did you sell the cigarettes to the detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were popular among the detainees; they knew you, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, they were not my debtors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were popular, you were known. Detainees knew you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, they knew me. Those who knew me, they knew me, and the others --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're the person who served the food --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence of Mr. Zigic objects because these are classical examples of leading questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Waidyaratne, [In English] if you see -- sorry. [Interpretation] If you look, you said, "You were popular, you were known." That is an assertion. You have to put the question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Very well. I will rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The detainees, according to you, have seen you many times, is that correct, because you served food to them and gave them water, according to what you said today.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the detainees knew you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Zoran Zigic gave you the cigarettes, did you go and sell it to anybody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. When he gave me two packets, I left them for myself, those two packets.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Please bear with me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I hope I have understood what you said in your direct examination. Did Zoran Zigic give you cigarettes to sell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sell those cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To whom did you sell those cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: There weren't that many cigarettes. There may have been three or four packets of cigarettes, of Kent cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These three or four packets - I'm sorry to take much time - but please, to whom did you sell these cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I sold them to my neighbours from Puharska and other people who I didn't know. I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have money with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: They did. If they didn't have money, I don't know how they would have been able to buy cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the price of the cigarettes that you sold to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, really, I can't remember now what the price was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you collect the money that you sold the cigarettes and give back to Mr. Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a substantial amount that you gave to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. Well, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did you sell cigarettes for Mr. Zigic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Waidyaratne, excuse me, but "substantial" is a qualification, and if the witness says yes or no, one doesn't know what is meant. "Do you have any idea as to the amount of money you earned?" I know the answer already, but put the question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember or recall the amount of money that you handed over to Mr. Zigic during that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I will go on. Now, Witness, did you sell food to the detainees while you were in the camp; biscuits?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who provided the food to you to be sold to the detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I don't know. A guard called me from down there, and every shift there was a new set of guards, and they forced me. I don't know his name. I know he was heavily built, balding, and he forced me to take those bags of food, to sell them, and to bring him the money. I had to do it, even if it was a bag of food that my own mother had brought for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you sold it to the detainees who had money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at any time were you asked to go into the room and call out for some detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you collect any items from the injured detainees from the rooms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. I collected those things in the rooms that were bloody. I collected those things and threw them on a truck. Because I had to wash that dormitory, and I washed it, so I collected these things with my own hands, and they were bloodied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, do you recall a person by the name of Spija Mesic who wore a pair of track shoes and a track suit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you come to know him in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: There were so many of them wearing track suits. I don't remember him. There were quite a lot of us there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if the witness gives a clear answer, saying that he doesn't know such-and-such a person, then I really don't see the purpose of the question whether that person was wearing a track suit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Waidyaratne. You asked the witness whether he knew him. The witness said no. Then you asked whether he came to know him in the camp. That only has sense if you put it this way: Upon your arrival, did you know that person? And the witness says no. And did you meet him later? That has sense. Otherwise we're turning round in a circle and wasting very precious time, as you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I will take your -- I realise the difficulty there, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said in the rooms that -- which was there bloody. Am I -- did I understand you correctly? What was -- what did you find in the rooms which was bloody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. Only in number 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has already answered the question. Actually, Mr. President, I really do regret for interrupting the cross-examination by the Prosecution. However, in answer to a question put by the Prosecutor a moment ago, the witness said that in one room he was cleaning the blood, and the question put by the Prosecutor was in the plural; in which rooms did he clean the blood. So I do appeal to my learned friend from the Prosecution to be more precise in his questions, because otherwise the witness really can be confused and he may give the wrong answer to the question put to him as a result of being misled.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: May I -- Your Honour, I think Mr. Deretic's objection is not well founded. At page 81, line 25, answer: "No. I collected those things in the rooms that were bloody." That's why I wanted to clarify. Thank you, Your Honour. I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue, but in any event, I think that all the interruptions that are not justified cause wasting time. The witness is here. He can always answer. I don't think that the witness is confused. He knows how to answer the questions. He was there. Let us show him at least that much respect. So please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, today when you gave -- in your direct examination you were shown Exhibit D4/8 [sic]; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I apologise, but I didn't see this map well. I can show you now. I put number 2 instead of number 3. Number 2 was right next to it. I can see it now on the screen, and the 4 was over here, so I made a mistake on this sketch. I didn't see it well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think you were talking for D8/4. It is the confusion that we referred to regarding the numbering, but it was recorded as D8/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I stand corrected, Your Honour. Thank you. I'm referring to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The witness has given an answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the photograph -- or the exhibit which is on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I didn't mark it properly. I didn't see it well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness wants to correct certain markings which he has done. I would ask him the questions, and if he wants to make a correction, could he mark in the same exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a question that perhaps the Defence should answer as well, but I think it would be better to use another photograph. If the Defence has another photograph, that would be better, so as to avoid any confusion. Otherwise, there will be several marks, one on top of another, and we will be confused. So perhaps it would be better to use another photograph, if Defence counsel has one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We quite agree that correction should be made. I have the original photograph from which the copies were made, and I will gladly give it to the usher to give it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I will ask the questions from the exhibit which is now before the witness. If there is any correction, it can be done in the re-examination, but I will put my question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So very well. The corrections will be made by the Defence counsel. So go on with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please look at the Exhibit D8/4, which is -- you marked Room 2 in that exhibit. Isn't that the wrong place that you have marked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you shown this exhibit before, before you saw it in the courtroom today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. I know Keraterm. I know Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. My question was: Did the Defence counsel show this exhibit to you before you came to the courthouse, the Chamber, today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. But I know Keraterm very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show Room 1, the correct place. Which is Room 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Here it is, on the corner, and number 2 is right next to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the exhibit which is on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point to the Room 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Keep the pointer there, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm just on my feet to try and assist the Trial Chamber and my learned friend. You see that the witness didn't quite understand. He could either use the pointer or his finger to point out Room 1. He didn't quite understand what he was supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Deretic. It is the Prosecutor's turn to put the questions. He knows whether he's satisfied with the answers or not. During your re-examination, you will be asking the questions, but thank you anyway. So please continue, Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please point to Room 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Waidyaratne, I think it should be borne in mind that the witness doesn't have the abilities that you have. He doesn't have experience with the use of these audiovisual devices, so you must be very precise in your question. "Could you point with the pointer on the ELMO where is 'X'," that you want him to do. If you tell him, "Show us point 'X'," he has in front of him the monitor, as you know. So his natural reaction is to point at the monitor and not at the document under the ELMO. So please give the witness the proper information he needs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I'm just asking another question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was Room 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Right next to number 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the places that you have marked in Exhibit D8/4 in the morning in your direct examination, that is incorrect; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. I got confused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point Room 3?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Excuse me. I didn't understand that at all, to the 2. If the witness could point to where Room 2 is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you kindly point to Room 2 again, please, Room 2, with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct if I say that Room 1 and 2 were adjoined?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now could you, to assist the Chamber, point to Room 3, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in that photograph exhibit you see, onto the left side of the place that you're pointing, another entrance. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Onto the left side.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a toilet there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, the toilet was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the entrance to the toilet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Right next to number "3". Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in the morning, in your direct examination, where you have marked number "3" is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Incorrect, incorrect. I should have put number "4" there, and where number "2" is, I should have put number "3", and number "1" should have been right in front of the first dormitory and number "2" right next to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Waidyaratne. Witness DD/1, and where you put "4", what should be there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: It should be dormitory number "4". No, the containers were over there. Where I put the number "4" is where the containers and the pallets were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. That's fine now. Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Just to follow up from the question that Your Honour put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the place where you went and put the bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the place where you say -- which you have marked already as number "4"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Behind the pallets here, that's where I put the bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's where you have marked number "4", correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Are there any pallets here? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, the place. Could you point it out on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I put them here, behind the pallets, between the pallets. And there was a garbage can here, and I put them here and here, behind the pallets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Witness, you spoke about an incident that took place in Room 3, the shooting at Room 3. You can't exactly remember when this incident happened, can you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, no. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you be able to recall some incidents before this shooting took place? You said that the people who were brought in were from the Brdo area or from --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when were they brought in? Can you remember? Now, we will fix the date. We will say before the shooting. How many days prior to the shooting were they brought in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I don't remember. I know they spent a long time in number 3 before the shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A long time in the sense of days; one, two, three?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how many days it was because I was only counting the days till I got out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, so you don't remember, but they were in there in Room 3 for some time? That's your position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when these people were brought in, do you remember -- were you tasked to collect the documents, any documents from these people who were brought into the camp, the detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you not tasked to burn the documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, no. No, I wasn't tasked either to collect or to burn the documents. I don't know who said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anybody burning any documents which were collected from these people who were brought in from the Brdo area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If it wasn't the soldiers in the buses when they rounded them up in Brdo --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Maybe the soldiers asked for their documents on the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. My question was: Did you see in the camp anybody collecting any documents from the people who were brought into the camp from the Brdo area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has already answered no, Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do so, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said the day of the shooting, in the morning, that you provided or distributed food, the breakfast, to the detainees in Room 3. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, a day before the shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they brought out? Were the detainees in Room 3 brought out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. They had gone wild.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why? Could you explain it to the Chamber, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, they went crazy. They just went mad. I know when I brought food to them, I opened the door once, but the next time I didn't dare because they grabbed my hands and tried to pull me in. They wanted to pull me in. God knows what might have happened to me. Then I broke the window up there. I didn't ask for soldiers or anyone. I threw in bags of food, and the food that my mother or my sister brought to me I would throw in to them, and they were grabbing for the food, fighting over it. They had gone mad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it your position, when you say that they had gone mad, that these people were not let out of that room to eat that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, because they started banging on the door, trying to run away. They damaged the door. They kicked it and punched it and pulled it out and then they started escaping.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time was this? Was it before you provided the breakfast, according to you, or was it in the evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, no. It was before breakfast was to be distributed to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, before this date, did you provide them food? Did you provide food to the people who were detained in Room 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they behave the same way when you provided the food to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, again, I was afraid to approach them. I was afraid to approach them and hand it to them directly. I was afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain it to us. Were they let out at all after they were put into Room 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know -- now, we'll go before that. I think -- I'm sorry to go back a step. Do you remember the camp -- the people who were in Room 3, before these people arrived, being sent to other rooms and clearing up Room 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I don't remember. I know that Rooms 1 and 2 and 4 were dormitories and then number 3 was opened up later on. Because number 4 used to be a prison for soldiers, and then the soldiers were moved to a place behind Keraterm for detention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, so when you said that you provided breakfast to the detainees in Room 3 in the morning of the shooting that happened in the night, what you said was not that they were allowed to come out and have what they were provided, but you simply threw it from a window, is that correct, a broken window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of these people who were detained in Room 3 who was brought in from that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That day, did you supply food to the other people who were detained in Room 1 and 2 and number 4?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: 1, 2, and 4, they went out to have breakfast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any beatings during the day of the shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you spoke about seeing machine-guns. Are you talking about the machine-guns which were permanently in the camp, or were any machine-guns put up temporarily that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: They were there temporarily when we came into the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were talking about the machine-guns that were there when you came into the camp; that's your position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if it's correct, it's more or less permanently, which has been there for some time, if I may use that word; not temporarily, but it has been there for some time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the day of the shooting, did you see any new guns being set up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you walk around that day in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until what time were you allowed to walk around that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, as long as I wanted to. So I went to the dormitory and then a guard would come to lock me in, and then he would lock us in and leave us in the dormitory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, is it correct if I say that you were one who was allowed to walk around, but all the other detainees couldn't come out of the rooms whenever they wanted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. Rooms 1 and 2 and 4, they could also go out, the same way I did, but I walked around more in the compound. They would go out to go to the toilet or have a drink of water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that the people -- the detainees in the Rooms 1, 2, and if I may miss 3, say 4, were allowed to come out of their rooms at any time of the day to go out, even to the toilet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. They would call a guard when they needed to go to the toilet. The guard would come, unlock the door, escort them to the toilet, and bring them back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But whereas you were allowed to move around freely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, that day of the shooting, how long did you stay out? Surely this must be on your mind.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: I?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: While there was shooting?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the shooting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Not long. I was unwell. I had a stomachache and a headache. I went to sleep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that day you were not well, you went to sleep earlier; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was in Room 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see as to what happened outside the rooms that evening or in the night; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: That's correct. I didn't see. I only know --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, next day, morning, you said that you were called out around 6.00 by [redacted]; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So weren't you afraid to go out after you heard so much of, you know, shooting the previous night till dawn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, there was no shooting just before dawn. When [redacted] came to fetch me to go, I saw from number 3, I saw how they had damaged the door and started fleeing. I saw them in front and near the toilet. You could see it from Room 1. And they were starting to run towards the fence, and I saw two who were dead and I saw that there were corpses lying around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you're talking about the dead people in the compound, am I correct, after the shooting? Now, you speak so well. Could you tell us: When you went to the Room 3, was another person by the name of Sead Jakupovic with you from Room 1, a detainee?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: With me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A detainee.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: What name did you say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sead Jakupovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. That's a neighbour of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He also went -- he was also asked to come out to help to load the bodies; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, but he couldn't do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I will ask -- we will go step by step. Witness, did you see the people who were killed and wounded inside the Room 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you gradually take out the bodies and lay it out in the compound in front of Room 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. First I collected the bodies, and those that were in front of Room 3, I lined them up, and then I went for the wounded and I put them there. And then I went into Room 3, this man I mentioned and I, Elkaz, the one I mentioned. He and I carried them, and he and I loaded them.
