And then my hands, my arms, my mouth, everything was covered with blood. My arms were bloody up to the elbows. I wish someone had taken a photograph of me. And it made me so sick I couldn't eat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did the people ask for water, people who were wounded ask for water, and did you give water to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I gave them water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And subsequently even the wounded were loaded into the truck and sent away; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. Both the wounded and the dead. I loaded them, all together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this would have taken some time to take out the bodies and to load them into the truck, because there were many; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes, but it didn't take long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, after that did -- you spoke about the incident where the truck came back and the truck was washed. Did you see the place being washed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: My brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he wash the area in front of the Room 3 or was it only the truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. Only the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: May I briefly go into a private session just to ask a couple of questions, Your Honour? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let us go into private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We're in public session. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If Your Honour will bear with me for a moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, now, we have heard much about how you helped in providing the -- distributing the food and the water. Now, what else did the guards ask you? You said once that you were asked to take the bodies and place the dead people, the detainees, behind Room 4; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did you do this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, whenever a man was killed, I carried him there. No one did that except for me and that other man, no one. And those who were here before and who said that this man had been with me and loaded bodies, that wasn't true. No one dared approach the corpses. Everybody was afraid when I called to them to come and help me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or was it the Serb authorities or the people who were in the camp had much confidence in you? They had confidence in you; is that correct? They selected you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any special reason for them to, you know, select you for this kind of work? Did you know any people in authority in the camp other than Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Deretic. Mr. Waidyaratne, please check the wording of your question. You're making a substantial assertion. I think that is what Mr. Deretic was going to object to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I will withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but Mr. Waidyaratne, at this stage of the trial you have to be careful.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I will withdraw that, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any other person in the camp other than Mr. Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes. Before the camp. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the camp, the people, the guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who asked you to do these jobs, these things that you have told us today, the taking of the dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, whoever managed to do it first. Whoever told me to carry a body, I had to do it, because if I didn't do it, they would have killed me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that Mr. Zoran Zigic once saved your life. Were there any other instances where Mr. Zigic helped, other than providing cigarettes, when you were in the Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Well, before that Zigic saved my life. If it hadn't been for Zigic, I would be dead now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Zigic there to protect you during the time that you spent in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: No. When Zigic was there that first time, then he saved my life. And then I saw Zigic only once, when Car was brought in. After that I didn't see him in mid-June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you only speak about two instances where you have seen Mr. Zigic; is that correct? Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you spent in the Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Waidyaratne, I think we have to adjourn for today. I don't know whether there is a good moment for you, but we have been working since quarter past one, more or less, so we have to break until tomorrow. I'm going to ask the usher - just a moment - to see the witness out first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask the English booth to switch off the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll be here again tomorrow at 9.20.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, before you leave, I have to make an objection. As the witness was passing by counsel's table, I saw Mr. Deretic say something to the witness. I could not say what Mr. Deretic said, but I certainly saw his mouth moving. I would ask the Trial Chamber -- I believe there is a no-contact order between counsel and the witnesses once the witness has begun his or her testimony. That has always been the policy of this Chamber. I would simply ask that counsel be cautioned, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I really don't know what to say. My mouth is so dry that I would like to drink a glassful of water. I was expecting the end, and there was just a gesture that I made and my learned friend thought I said something, and I didn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the witness leaves, could the witness look at the Judges. I don't know. If we're going to be in such a strict position, then it will be very difficult for us to work. But I trust you to know what we should do and we should not do. I trust people. People are adults. But I'm telling you if there are any infractions, the Chamber is here. But I think that we must trust one another after all, otherwise, we will all become paranoid. Every gesture or a word which may be uttered by chance may be given unnecessary value and that will place us in an impossible situation to work. Let us be reasonable, let us act as adults, and above all, and above all, and I insist on this, let us be good professionals, respecting our ethics and the rules, and in my opinion, that should be sufficient for us to be able to complete our work properly, because my concern is not only to do a lot of work but also to do it well, because as you know, it is sometimes very difficult to make a proper balance between the quantity and the quality of work. But I prefer to have good quality work that is based on human qualities and the professional qualities of the persons here present. I always have in mind for somebody to be a good professional, he first of all has to be a humane person and then technically qualified. And not a professor. I'm just sharing with you my view of things. I'm just sharing with you my view of things and reality and life. To be a humane person, technically qualified. We have diplomas qualifying us to work in this courtroom. Having said that, we will adjourn until tomorrow at 9.20.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I really don't know to whom this photograph on the ELMO belongs. Can we pick it up? It's still there.
